business.title: Bitcoin forms key 'head and shoulders' pattern ...
business.description: Bitcoin is currently forming an inverse head-and-shoulders pattern on its price chart, with a crucial resistance level at $67,200. This pattern suggests a potential reversal after a significant drop from May highs above $81,000. Ethereum, meanwhile, has already broken out of a similar pattern and is moving upward, indicating stronger momentum. Bitcoin's next few days will be decisive: a move above $67,200 could confirm a bullish reversal, while failure to break this level may lead to further declines toward $60,000 or $58,000 support levels.

business.title: Bitcoin tests $63,500 resistance, risks dipping...
business.description: Bitcoin is currently facing resistance near $63,500, with a risk of a short-term drop to the $60,000-$61,100 support zone if sellers regain control. This could trigger a liquidity sweep below $62,000 before a potential rebound. A long-term cycle model forecasts a deeper bottom between $40,000 and $45,000 in 2026, followed by a possible bull run reaching $215,000 to $230,000 by 2029. Investors should watch the $60,000 demand zone closely for signs of the next major move, while the long-term outlook remains cautiously bullish despite potential near-term volatility.

science.title: In 2003, scientists found Chile's Atacama desert so dry it had no detectable DNA. Now it's helping prepare for Mars missions
science.description: Chile's Atacama Desert serves as Earth's closest Mars analogue due to its extreme dryness. This arid environment, with minimal rainfall and biological activity, aids planetary research. Scientists study its soil chemistry and extreme conditions to prepare for Mars missions. Discoveries there have refined strategies for detecting life on the Red Planet. The Atacama Desert continues to be a vital natural laboratory for space exploration.
